topic: PWM for LED dimming and motor speed
title: Fade an LED with PWM
instructions:
## Brightness without an analogue output

A microcontroller pin is either HIGH or LOW, but switching it fast with a varying duty cycle (**pulse-width modulation**) makes an LED look dimmer or brighter. `analogWrite(pin, value)` sets the duty cycle from 0 (always off) to 255 (always on) on a PWM pin.

## Do this

Fade the LED on pin 9 smoothly from off to full brightness and back down, repeatedly. Use a `for` loop (or a variable that counts up and down) with a short `delay(10)` between steps. The check wants at least 20 different levels and the value reaching both 0 and 255.
hints: analogWrite(9, brightness); then brightness = brightness + step;
When brightness reaches 0 or 255, reverse: step = -step;
delay(10) between steps gives a half-second fade each way.

checks.label: Pin 9 fades through many levels, from 0 to 255

realityNote: Only the pins marked with ~ on an Uno can do PWM (3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 11), at about 490 Hz or 980 Hz. The same trick drives a DC motor through a transistor or H-bridge, which cannot be done with a plain resistor.
